\section[o aeroporto]{o aeroporto — an airport}

\label{lesson:PT-C85-aeroporto}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for that is why, then the Portuguese for a cause.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o aeroporto}
\textbf{o aeroporto} — \textquotedblleft{}an airport\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{aeroporto} is built from \emph{aero-}, \textquotedblleft{}air\textquotedblright{}, from Greek \emph{aēr}, and \emph{porto}, \textquotedblleft{}port\textquotedblright{} $\leftarrow$ Latin \emph{portus}, \textquotedblleft{}harbour\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB 2.1).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[a paragem]{a paragem — a stop (bus, tram)}

\label{lesson:PT-C85-paragem}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a paragem}
\textbf{a paragem} — \textquotedblleft{}a stop (bus, tram)\textquotedblright{}. In Brazil, \textbf{o ponto}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{paragem} is built from the verb \textquotedblleft{}to stop\textquotedblright{} and \emph{-agem}. That verb $\leftarrow$ Latin \emph{parare}, \textquotedblleft{}to prepare, to make ready\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB 2.1).
\end{cousinweb}

\end{cousinweb}

\section[a câmara municipal]{a câmara municipal — a town hall}

\label{lesson:PT-C85-camara-municipal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the post office, then the Portuguese for a cinema.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a câmara municipal}
\textbf{a câmara municipal} — \textquotedblleft{}a town hall\textquotedblright{}. In Brazil, \textbf{a prefeitura}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{câmara municipal} is \textquotedblleft{}municipal chamber\textquotedblright{}: \emph{câmara} $\leftarrow$ Latin \emph{camera}, \textquotedblleft{}vaulted room\textquotedblright{}, from Greek \emph{kamara} (EtymDB 2.1), and \emph{municipal} $\leftarrow$ Latin \emph{municipalis}, \textquotedblleft{}of a free town\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}
